description: Filtered turbidity has been creeping up all week and the duty filter has been running since Monday. Headloss gauge reads higher than usual. Nothing else seems off.

expected.diagnosis: Duty filter is due for backwash: turbidity reached 0.25 NTU after a long run with rising headloss. Normal end of a filter run.
key_steps: Backwash the duty filter now since turbidity hit the 0.25 NTU trigger (Manual 2.2)
Backwash 10–15 minutes until waste runs clear, then filter-to-waste until below 0.15 NTU (Manual 2.3)
Recheck turbidity at 1 hour and 4 hours and record new clean-filter headloss (Manual 2.4)

description: Chlorine was fine all week but this morning it's only 0.35. The day tank looks almost empty.

expected.diagnosis: Hypochlorite day tank ran low, so the feed pump is drawing air or not enough solution. Low residual, but above the 0.2 mg/L emergency limit.
key_steps: Mix a fresh batch: 1 gallon of 12.5% hypochlorite, filled to the 20-gallon mark (Manual 3.2)
Check the feed pump is primed and bleed air if needed (Manual 7.3)
Retest chlorine 30 minutes after refilling (Manual 3.2)

description: Chlorine dropped to 0.15 this morning. The hypochlorite pump is running but there's solution leaking around the pump head. I tried priming it twice and it didn't help.

expected.diagnosis: Hypochlorite feed pump has a failed diaphragm, so almost no chlorine is being fed. Residual is below the 0.2 mg/L EPA minimum.
key_steps: Switch to the standby hypochlorite feed pump right away (Manual 3.3)
Contact the RMW now — residual is below 0.2 mg/L (Manual 3.3, 8.1)
If residual is not back to 0.2 mg/L within 4 hours, notify ADEC and prepare for a boil-water notice (Manual 3.3, 8.2)

description: Chlorine has been dropping a little every day this week. It's still above the action level so I haven't done anything. The batch in the day tank was mixed about 12 days ago. The plant has been warm.

expected.diagnosis: Slow chlorine drift from an old hypochlorite batch losing strength in a warm room. Still above 0.5 mg/L, but the 7-day decline needs action now.
key_steps: Treat the multi-day decline as a problem even though it's in range (Manual 3.5)
Mix a fresh batch since the current one is older than 7 days (Manual 3.2)
Inspect the feed pump diaphragm and check valve (Manual 3.5)
Retest 30 minutes after the new batch and log the trend (Manual 3.2, 1.3)

description: Breakup started on the lake this week and the raw water is brown. I've backwashed twice a day but filtered turbidity keeps climbing. Online meter says 1.3 this morning and the bench meter agrees.

steps_taken: Increased turbidity checks to every 4 hours

expected.diagnosis: Spring breakup raw water is overwhelming the filters. Bench meter confirms filtered turbidity above the 1.0 NTU EPA limit.
key_steps: Stop sending the filter's water to the clearwell if possible (Manual 4.3)
Contact the RMW immediately and ADEC within 24 hours (Manual 4.3, 8.1)
Prepare for a boil-water notice since turbidity is above 1.0 NTU (Manual 8.2, 8.3)

description: Breakup is happening and filter runs are way shorter — I'm backwashing about every 30 hours instead of 3 days. Filtered turbidity has been in the 0.2s. Is something wrong?

expected.diagnosis: Short filter runs are expected during spring breakup. Filtered turbidity is elevated but under 0.3 NTU, and backwashing brings it down.
key_steps: Keep backwashing as needed — short runs are expected during breakup (Manual 2.2)
Backwash now since turbidity is above 0.25 NTU (Manual 2.3)
Confirm with the bench meter, check the coagulant pump, and test every 4 hours (Manual 4.2)

description: pH has gone up every day this week and is 8.3 today. Chlorine looks normal. I changed the soda ash batch last Sunday.

expected.diagnosis: Soda ash overfeed, probably from a stronger new batch, has pushed pH above 8.0. That reduces how well chlorine works, but it's still inside 6.5–8.5.
key_steps: Calibrate the pH meter with pH 7 and pH 10 buffers to confirm the reading (Manual 5.1)
Lower the soda ash pump stroke in 5% steps (Manual 5.3)
Keep chlorine in the upper half of the target range until pH is below 7.8 (Manual 5.3)

description: pH keeps dropping and it's 6.3 today. The soda ash pump is humming but the day tank level hasn't moved in days.

expected.diagnosis: Soda ash feed pump isn't delivering, so pH has fallen below 6.5. Corrosive water can release lead and copper.
key_steps: Contact the RMW — pH is below 6.5 (Manual 5.4, 8.1)
Bleed air from the soda ash pump and check the foot valve and suction line for crystals (Manual 7.3)
Once feeding, raise the soda ash stroke in 5% steps and retest after 1 hour (Manual 5.2)

description: Loop return temp alarm went off at 37°F overnight. The duty circ pump wasn't running. I switched to the standby pump and the temp is back up to 42°F. It's -20°F outside.

expected.diagnosis: Duty circulation pump stopped, so loop return temperature dropped. The standby pump restored circulation in time with no loss of service.
key_steps: Keep running on the standby circulation pump and recheck return temperature after 1 hour (Manual 6.2)
Check the duty pump's breaker and overload before trying it again (Manual 7.2)
Log the event (Manual 1.3)

description: It's -35°F. The north end of the loop stopped circulating sometime last night, probably 4 or 5 hours ago, and the school says their water pressure is very low. Circ pumps at the plant are both running.

expected.diagnosis: Likely frozen main on the north loop. Circulation has been lost for more than 2 hours in extreme cold, and pressure loss at the school risks contamination.
key_steps: Contact the RMW immediately — loss of circulation over 2 hours with a likely frozen line (Manual 6.4, 8.1)
Check distribution pressure; below 20 psi is a boil-water notice trigger (Manual 7.4, 8.2)
Contact ADEC about a boil-water notice for the affected area (Manual 8.3)

description: The online turbidimeter has read exactly 0.05 for five days. That seems too good. The bench meter read 0.25 this morning. It was -25°F last night.

expected.diagnosis: Frozen turbidimeter sample line is giving a false, unchanging reading. Actual filtered turbidity from the bench meter is 0.25 NTU, at the backwash trigger.
key_steps: Thaw the sample line with heat trace or a heat gun (no open flame) and flush 10 minutes (Manual 6.3)
Trust the bench meter and recalibrate the online meter since they differ by more than 0.1 NTU (Manual 4.4)
Backwash since actual turbidity reached 0.25 NTU (Manual 2.2, 2.3)

description: Raw water pump 1 wouldn't start this morning and the clearwell level was dropping. Breaker was tripped. I reset it and it's running fine now. Readings look normal.

expected.diagnosis: Tripped breaker on raw water pump 1. It was reset successfully with no water quality impact.
key_steps: Switch to the standby raw water pump first whenever the duty pump fails (Manual 7.2)
If the breaker trips again right after reset, leave it off and contact the RMW (Manual 7.2)
Log the event so repeat trips are visible (Manual 1.3)

description: Filter 2 turbidity is high again — 0.42 this morning even though I backwashed it twice yesterday. This keeps happening.

log_history.problem: Filter 2 turbidity high after short run
Filter 2 turbidity high, third time this month
log_history.outcome: Turbidity 0.22 NTU, still higher than normal

expected.diagnosis: Recurring filter 2 problem — likely media loss, mudballs, or underdrain damage. Turbidity stays above 0.3 NTU after two backwashes, and the problem has happened at least 3 times in 30 days.
key_steps: Contact the RMW for a filter inspection — repeat problem and above 0.3 NTU after two backwashes (Manual 2.5, 8.1)
Switch duty to filter 1 while waiting (Manual 2.1)
Test turbidity every 4 hours until below 0.15 NTU (Manual 4.2)

description: Chlorine was low on Tuesday so I turned the pump up. Now it's 2.4 and people at the washeteria say the water smells like bleach.

expected.diagnosis: Overcorrection after the low chlorine reading: the feed pump stroke was raised too far. Residual is above 2.0 mg/L, but well below the 4.0 mg/L limit.
key_steps: Lower the feed pump stroke in 5% steps and retest 30 minutes after each change (Manual 3.4)
Future increases: 5% steps, no more than 10% per hour (Manual 3.2)
Log the adjustment (Manual 1.3)

description: Chlorine is 4.3 today. I think the new batch was mixed with 2 gallons of bleach instead of 1 and the pump stroke was also turned up last week.

expected.diagnosis: Hypochlorite batch mixed too strong, combined with a high pump stroke. Residual is above EPA's 4.0 mg/L maximum residual disinfectant level.
key_steps: Stop the hypochlorite feed pump (Manual 3.4)
Contact the RMW — chlorine is above 4.0 mg/L (Manual 3.4, 8.1)
Do not restart until residual is below 2.0 mg/L; remix the batch correctly with 1 gallon (Manual 3.4, 3.2)

description: Since the lake turned over last week, I'm backwashing every day and a half. Turbidity stays under 0.25 most of the time. Raw water smells a bit earthy.

expected.diagnosis: Fall lake turnover is raising raw water turbidity and shortening filter runs. This is expected seasonal behavior, and filtered water is staying in range.
key_steps: Keep backwashing at the 0.25 NTU, 8 psi, or 72-hour trigger — short runs are normal during turnover (Manual 2.2)
Check raw water and confirm the coagulant pump is running (Manual 4.2)
Do not change the coagulant dose yourself; ask the RMW about a jar test if runs keep shortening (Manual 2.1)

description: Monday morning chlorine is 0.4. The day tank level hasn't gone down since Saturday. There was a power blip Saturday night.

log_history.outcome: Chlorine back to 1.0 mg/L within an hour

expected.diagnosis: Hypochlorite feed pump lost prime, likely after the power blip — the day tank level hasn't changed. One earlier occurrence a month ago is not a recurring pattern yet.
key_steps: Open the bleed valve and run the pump until solution flows with no bubbles (Manual 7.3)
Check the foot valve and suction line for air leaks (Manual 7.3)
Retest chlorine 30 minutes after restoring prime (Manual 3.2)
After power outages, confirm chemical feed pumps restarted (Manual 7.5)

description: Chlorine is low again, 0.45 today. I mixed a fresh batch and primed the pump on Tuesday and it came back up, but now it's dropping again.

expected.diagnosis: Recurring low chlorine — the 4th time in about 3 weeks. Fixes only work temporarily, which suggests a failing pump, check valves, or a suction leak. Readings are above 0.2, but the recurrence requires escalation.
key_steps: Contact the RMW — the same problem has happened 3 or more times in 30 days (Manual 8.1)
Replace the feed pump check valves with the spare kit (Manual 7.3)
Inspect the pump diaphragm and log the trend (Manual 3.5, 1.3)

description: Online turbidity has crept up from 0.12 to 0.28 over the week. I just backwashed on Wednesday and headloss is low. The bench meter reads 0.11.

expected.diagnosis: The online turbidimeter has drifted out of calibration. The bench meter shows filtered water is actually fine at 0.11 NTU.
key_steps: Recalibrate the online turbidimeter with fresh standards — it differs from the bench meter by more than 0.1 NTU (Manual 4.4)
No backwash needed since actual turbidity is below 0.25 NTU (Manual 2.2)
Keep comparing online and bench readings daily (Manual 4.4)

description: Houses at the top of the hill say pressure is weak in the evenings. The gauge at the high point read 28 psi at dinnertime. The high-service pump seems to be cycling on and off a lot.

expected.diagnosis: High-service pump is short-cycling, likely a pressure switch problem, causing low evening pressure at the high point. Pressure is below 35 psi but above the 20 psi trigger.
key_steps: Switch to the standby high-service pump (Manual 7.2)
Check the pressure switch and look for leaks or main breaks (Manual 7.4, 7.2)
If pressure falls below 20 psi anywhere, it's a boil-water notice trigger (Manual 7.4, 8.2)
